record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.original_question: For Stable Marriage instances with uncertain preferences in the lottery model, determine the computational complexity of SM HighestProbability: compute a matching with the highest probability of being stable when each agent has a probability distribution over strict preference lists.

evidence.quote: 2. PO / SM HighestProbability: Compute a matching with the highest probability of being Pareto optimal / stable.
Question marks denote the open cases.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Stable Marriage problem with uncertain preferences in the lottery model, defined as follows. There are two disjoint finite sets of agents, men M and women W, with |M| = |W| = n. Each agent a ∈ M ∪ W is associated with a probability distribution P_a over the set of strict (linear) preference orders on the agents of the opposite side; the distributions of different agents are independent. A realization is obtained by independently sampling, for each agent a, a strict preference list according to P_a. Given a perfect matching μ between M and W, the matching is said to be stable in a realization if there is no blocking pair, i.e., no pair (m, w) ∈ M × W with μ(m) ≠ w such that m strictly prefers w to μ(m) and w strictly prefers m to μ(w) under the realized preferences. The stability probability of μ is the probability, over the random realization, that μ is stable.

Problem (SM-HighestProbability, lottery model): Given the distributions {P_a}_{a ∈ M ∪ W} as input, determine the computational complexity of the problem of computing a perfect matching μ that maximizes the stability probability. In particular, decide whether this optimization problem (or its natural decision version: given a rational threshold q, does there exist a matching whose stability probability is at least q?) is solvable in polynomial time, NP-hard, or of some other complexity.
artifact.status_search_result: The general complexity of SM-HighestProbability in the lottery model appears to remain open. Partial results are known: the problem is NP-hard in restricted settings (e.g., under certain transitivity/WST assumptions), and it is polynomial-time solvable when only a constant number of agents on the same side are uncertain. No full classification (polynomial-time algorithm or unconditional NP-hardness) for the general lottery model has been reported.

status_evidence.title: Stable Matching with Uncertain Linear Preferences
status_evidence.snippet: The complexity of MatchingWithHighestStabilityProbability in the lottery model is not known in general, except when only a constant number of agents are uncertain on the same side of the market.
status_evidence.claim: General complexity in the lottery model is open; tractable in restricted cases.

status_evidence.title: Stable Matching with Uncertain Linear Preferences (arXiv)
status_evidence.snippet: StabilityProbability is #P-complete for the lottery model; MatchingWithHighestStabilityProbability is NP-hard under certain transitivity assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: NP-hardness shown only in restricted variants; the general lottery-model case remains unresolved.
